prompt: Stage 2-5, level 4 with 7 gold and 94 HP. You hold a pair of a 2-cost AD carry and a pair of a 2-cost AP caster on the bench, from two different lines, plus a Bow and a Sword. The shop shows a third copy of each at 2 gold, and the standard level 5 costs 4. Your scout shows two players already on the caster's line and nobody on the carry's. What do you buy?

lobby.note: 2-star of your AP caster with two AP components
Pair of your AP caster on the bench, a Rod on a placeholder
Tanks and a 1-cost AD reroll, holding a Vest

options.label: Buy the AD carry copy (2), level to 5 (4), and field the 2-star with the Bow and Sword on it; keep the caster pair on the bench
Buy the caster copy: a 2-star caster is the stronger unit this round
Buy both copies (4 gold) and skip the level until 2-6
Buy neither and level: a flex opener means not choosing until 3-2

explanation:
The AD carry copy gives you a 2-star that holds the Sword and the Bow this round, on a line nobody is on; the caster copy gives you a 2-star with no item that two players are already itemising, one of them ahead of you with a 2-star.

The arithmetic: a 2-cost has 25 copies. Your caster: Seat 3 holds 3, Seat 6 holds 2, you hold 2, so 18 remain for three players who all keep buying. Your AD carry: 23 remain and one buyer. Six gold here is a level and a 2-star that fits your items, and the caster pair stays on the bench, costing two slots and nothing else, until 3-2 confirms the read.

Buying both and skipping the level puts you a unit short for three fights at 2 to 4 HP each, for a bench 2-star with no slot to stand in. Buying neither confuses keeping options with refusing strength: a flex opener is the strongest board that still has two endgames.
principle: When two pairs compete for the same gold, buy the one your items and the empty pool already chose.
commonMistake: Making the 2-star that looks stronger this round instead of the one that holds your items and has nobody on it.
hint: Look at what each 2-star would hold this round, then count the copies of each unit that other players already have.
